title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality Characterization
description: Formalizes when equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz and Hölder inequalities. CS equality (∑fᵢgᵢ)² = (∑fᵢ²)(∑gᵢ²) iff proportional, proved via Lagrange identity. Extended to general Hölder: equality iff power proportionality fᵢ^p = c·gᵢ^q, proved via Young deficit reduction.

meta.historicalContext: The equality condition for Cauchy-Schwarz has been known since Cauchy (1821): equality holds iff the vectors are proportional. Lagrange's identity (1773) provides an elegant proof by expressing the CS deficit as a sum of squared cross-terms. For inner product spaces, the equality case is fundamental to projection theory and the Gram-Schmidt process.

sections.title: Lagrange Identity
sections.summary: Proves the Lagrange identity: the double sum of squared cross-terms (fᵢgⱼ - fⱼgᵢ)² equals twice the Cauchy-Schwarz deficit.

sections.title: Sum of Squares Zero Characterization
sections.summary: A sum of squares is zero iff each term is zero. Extended to double sums.

sections.title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality Characterization
sections.summary: Full iff: equality in CS holds iff all cross-terms fᵢgⱼ - fⱼgᵢ vanish, giving proportionality.

sections.title: Inner Product Space Equality
sections.summary: Abstract characterization: ‖inner u v‖ = ‖u‖·‖v‖ iff u = c•v, using Mathlib's norm_inner_eq_norm_iff.

sections.title: Hölder and Cauchy-Schwarz for Finite Sums
sections.summary: Hölder's inequality for NNReal sums and Cauchy-Schwarz as an independent consequence of the Lagrange identity.

sections.title: Conjugate Exponent Identities
sections.summary: Proves fundamental identities for Hölder conjugate exponents: q=p/(p-1), (p-1)(q-1)=1, q/p+1=q, 1<q, p+q=pq.

sections.title: Young's Equality Case
sections.summary: Defines the Young deficit a^p/p + b^q/q - ab and axiomatizes its equality characterization: deficit = 0 iff a^p = b^q.

sections.title: General Hölder Equality Characterization
sections.summary: Reduces Hölder equality to pointwise Young equality via sum-of-nonneg = 0 technique. Proves normalized case: ∑fᵢgᵢ = 1 implies fᵢ^p = gᵢ^q.

sections.title: Recovering Cauchy-Schwarz from Hölder
sections.summary: Shows p=q=2 power proportionality fᵢ² = c·gᵢ² reduces to linear proportionality fᵢ = √c·gᵢ for non-negative functions.

overview.summary: Characterizes equality in both Cauchy-Schwarz and general Hölder inequalities. CS: equality iff proportional (via Lagrange identity). Hölder: equality iff power proportionality fᵢ^p = c·gᵢ^q (via Young deficit reduction). Both use the same fundamental technique: a sum of non-negative quantities equals zero iff each is zero.
overview.keyIdea: A unifying technique: express the inequality deficit as a sum of non-negative terms. For CS, these are squared cross-terms (fᵢgⱼ-fⱼgᵢ)². For Hölder, these are Young deficits (fᵢ^p/p + gᵢ^q/q - fᵢgᵢ). In both cases, equality forces each term to vanish, yielding the characterization.

conclusion.summary: We formalize equality characterizations for both Cauchy-Schwarz and general Hölder inequalities. The CS case is fully proved via Lagrange identity with a complete iff characterization. The Hölder case is fully proved via Young deficit reduction, including both directions (equality ↔ power proportionality). The key insight is that both CS and Hölder equality follow from the same 'sum of nonneg = 0' technique.
openQuestions: Can the a.e. power proportionality condition for integral Hölder equality be formalized?
